image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey MK Restaurants suki hot pot outlet building, detailed front elevation with a wide glazed frontage showing booth tables under a green fascia carrying the MK roundel wordmark on an illuminated sign, a backlit photographic menu panel set flush beside the glass entrance door, plain warm cream painted side and rear walls in a single flat off-white tone clearly lighter than the background, with a kitchen service door and an extract grille, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: green painted composite panel and backlit printed menu face at the front, plate glass, flat warm cream painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant and extract ducting.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless MID-DARK neutral grey (#606060), distinctly darker than every part of the building so the object reads as a clean cut-out against it. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: MK Restaurants. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- not a pass self-score. 1740/16000 triangles, 10/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 10/16 unique geometries, 5 textures. Thirty-four more authored parts than the second build at the same draw-call and material count: every new part folded into an existing merge or the instanced unit.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7; turntable silhouette ratios 1.00 / 0.94 / 1.04 / 0.94 at 0/90/180/270 with no enclosed hole at any azimuth; +X side and roof rectified at 150 px/m (scratch/_mk/side_rect.png, roof_rect.png).
featureReviews.notes: Third build. The shell is now four boxes leaving the service-door pocket open; the shell face stays at z=3.22 (no canopy) so the depth is the declared 7.00. The roofline is broken by the two condensers and the ducted unit along the back wall, all under the 4.60 coping (unit top 4.33, condenser top 4.33). Meshy reads the plate 10% taller and 17% deeper than the declared module; the declaration is the kit's shared retail module across seven siblings and wins.

featureReviews.evidence: Round white disc (#F9FAF9, PBR confidence 0.833) proud of the green band and left of centre, carrying the plate's own roundel: red brush-script MK over small green RESTAURANTS, no ring, no band (sign/nb_sign.png, a Nano Banana 2 front-on redraw of the plate's sign crop).
featureReviews.notes: The second build drew a green ring and a green RESTAURANTS bar with Arial glyphs; the plate (scratch/_mk/sign_zoom.png) has neither -- a thin grey rim, a brush-script red MK and green outlined capitals. The redraw is baked as a 512 WebP on the CircleGeometry face, scaled 1.28x about the centre so the MK spans ~70% of the disc as on the plate; the canvas ops stay as the decode fallback.

featureReviews.evidence: Green panelling #396940 (PBR confidence 0.803) as five panel bays between joints at x -1.90/-0.63/0.63/1.90 over a lower rail row, pilasters at BOTH front corners split at 1.55 and 2.90, the +X pilaster returning 5 cm round the corner; 2.5 cm joints over a black backing.
featureReviews.notes: The second build carried the band as one flat slab and recorded the joints as below prop resolution. The plate's front (scratch/_mk/front_zoom.png) shows the joints clearly at hero distance, including a horizontal joint 0.8 of the way down the band; they are geometry now at zero extra draw calls (panels merge into front-feature, backings into the frame merge). The -X pilaster stops 1 cm short of the wall plane after check-coplanar flagged it flush.

featureReviews.evidence: Near-black powder-coated frame #3A3023 (PBR confidence 0.734): one butt-glazed window, one door bay with transom and pull bar, the lightbox border -- layout read off the rectified plate (sign/glass.png). Window and door are PLAIN tinted glass (#5C6C70 -> #46565A) and the menu poster survives only inside the lightbox rect.
featureReviews.notes: Rebuilt to the owner's brief: the baked interior view is gone. The glazing image is a flat blue-green tint with the plate's poster pasted only at x 2.30..3.10, y 0.14..2.22, so the lightbox still reads as a lit menu. The tint is held on chroma rather than lifted to grey: turntable gate found no enclosed hole at 0/90/180/270. Roughness 0.12 for the glass lobe.

featureReviews.evidence: Rectified +X elevation (scratch/_mk/side_rect.png, 150 px/m): door 0.95 m wide at 3.60..4.55 m from the front corner, louvre 1.25 x 0.75 m at 5.20..6.45 m, h 2.45..3.20. Built at world z -1.33..-0.38 (door, recessed 0.12 m in a reveal with jambs, head and lever) and z -3.23..-1.98 (two-panel louvre: 18 slats and a mullion over a black back plate).
featureReviews.notes: The second build had the louvre at z +0.95 -- towards the FRONT -- and a flush door slab; both were authored from the foreshortened plate. Per the brief the vent is now towards the rear and the door is inset. Deliberately NOT mirrored onto the -X wall, which the single plate does not show.

featureReviews.evidence: Two split condensers (0.90 x 0.66 x 0.34 casing, dark front plate, darker fan disc behind five light guard bars, vertex-toned, one instanced geometry) at x -3.05 / -1.95 and a 2.4 x 0.75 x 0.90 m ducted unit with 8 louvre slats over a black plate and a rounded +X hood, all against the rear parapet (z -3.22..-2.32) and under the 4.60 coping.
featureReviews.notes: The roof rectification (scratch/_mk/roof_rect.png) reads the plate's three units as two 0.9 m fan condensers and one 2.4 m ducted box with a curved end. The plate stands them mid-roof; the owner's brief puts them along the back wall, and that placement is built. The second build's three identical default casings, one of them standing in for the ducted box, are replaced by two real unit types at the same 10 draw calls.
